name: Plyboards & Laminates
tagline: The carcass and the surface stuck to it
description: Boards are the first specification decision on any interior job: they set the cost, the lifespan and how the joinery behaves in a damp Indian summer. What is pressed onto them decides how the job reads. This section runs from plywood by bonding grade and engineered boards like MDF and HDHMR, through high-pressure laminates organised the way designers actually shop — Brand, Collection, Design — to natural and reconstituted veneers, and the acrylic and PET panels used when a client wants mirror depth.

materials.name: MR plywood
materials.blurb: Moisture-resistant interior grade — the default for dry-area joinery
materials.description: Bonded with urea-formaldehyde resin, MR ply handles humidity but not standing water. It is the workhorse board for wardrobes, beds and TV units in dry rooms, and the cheapest plywood worth specifying on a paying job.

materials.name: BWR plywood
materials.blurb: Boiling-water-resistant grade for kitchens and utility joinery
materials.description: BWR uses phenolic resin, so it survives repeated wetting and drying far better than MR. Specify it wherever splashes are routine but full immersion is not — kitchen carcasses, utility storage and washbasin counters.

materials.name: BWP / Marine plywood
materials.blurb: Fully waterproof marine grade for wet areas and outdoor joinery
materials.description: The top bonding grade in the IS system, tested against 72 hours of boiling water. Worth the premium for sink units, bathroom vanities, balcony joinery and anything that will sit against an external wall.

materials.name: Commercial plywood
materials.blurb: Budget MR-grade board for backing panels and low-load work
materials.description: Lighter core, thinner face veneers and a lower price. Fine for back panels, shutters that carry no load and site-level temporary work — not for anything that must hold a hinge for a decade.

materials.name: Fire-retardant plywood
materials.blurb: Chemically treated board for escape routes and public interiors
materials.description: Impregnated with fire-retardant chemicals so flame spread is slowed and the board self-extinguishes. Commonly mandated in hotels, offices, hospitals and any interior work near an escape corridor.

materials.name: Flexible plywood
materials.blurb: Bends to a curve without steaming — for columns and curved fronts
materials.description: Cross-grain construction lets the sheet roll in one direction. Two layers laminated over a former give a stable curved panel for reception desks, curved bedbacks and column cladding.

materials.name: Shuttering plywood
materials.blurb: Film-faced board for concrete formwork, reusable many times
materials.description: A phenolic film face lets concrete release cleanly and survives repeated pours. On interior sites it also turns up as a rugged working surface and protection board during the messy trades.

materials.name: Blockboard
materials.blurb: Softwood-batten core — light and straight over long spans
materials.description: Strips of softwood sandwiched between veneers make a board that stays flat across a long shutter and weighs much less than ply. The classic choice for tall wardrobe shutters, door panels and long shelves.

materials.name: Calibrated plywood
materials.blurb: Sanded to an exact thickness — the base for veneer and laminate
materials.description: Machine-sanded to a tight thickness tolerance so pressed veneer or laminate lies perfectly flat with no telegraphing. Specify it whenever a high-gloss or veneered face has to look faultless.

materials.name: MDF
materials.blurb: Dense, uniform fibreboard — the surface for paint and routing
materials.description: No grain, no voids and a face smooth enough to spray directly. Ideal for CNC-routed panels, painted shutters and mouldings, but it swells badly if water reaches an unsealed edge.

materials.name: HDHMR
materials.blurb: High-density, high-moisture-resistant board — screws like ply, finishes like MDF
materials.description: A denser cousin of MDF made to hold fasteners and resist swelling. It has become the default modular-kitchen board where a laminate finish and good screw-holding both matter.

materials.name: HDF
materials.blurb: Very dense thin board for laminate flooring cores and back panels
materials.description: Denser and harder than MDF, usually seen as the core of laminate flooring or as a rigid thin back panel. Excellent surface hardness, poor tolerance of standing water.

materials.name: Particle board
materials.blurb: Lowest-cost engineered board for flat-pack and low-load furniture
materials.description: Wood chips bonded under pressure — cheap, flat and stable in dry conditions. Best kept to flat-pack furniture, office workstations and anywhere the budget will not stretch to HDHMR.

materials.name: Pre-laminated MDF
materials.blurb: MDF with the decorative face already pressed on — no site lamination
materials.description: Comes out of the factory finished on both faces, so carpentry is cut-and-assemble only. Saves days on fast-track jobs; the trade-off is a fixed palette and edges that must be banded.

materials.name: Pre-laminated particle board
materials.blurb: Factory-finished particle board for high-volume, low-cost furniture
materials.description: The cheapest finished board on the market and the backbone of budget office furniture. Specify with sealed edges and keep it well away from wet areas.

materials.name: WPC board
materials.blurb: Wood-plastic composite — termite-proof and genuinely waterproof
materials.description: A PVC-and-wood-flour composite that does not swell, rot or feed termites. It has largely replaced marine ply in bathroom vanities and balcony joinery, though it is softer and holds screws less firmly.

materials.name: PVC foam board
materials.blurb: Lightweight rigid foam sheet for wet zones and signage
materials.description: All plastic, zero moisture absorption, very light to handle. Good for bathroom shutters, service-duct covers and signage; not suitable where hinges and handles will see heavy daily load.

materials.name: OSB
materials.blurb: Oriented strand board — structural sheathing with a graphic face
materials.description: Large wood strands bonded in oriented layers make a strong, cheap structural sheet. In interiors it is used as an exposed finish in cafés, studios and industrial-look retail.

materials.name: Bamboo board
materials.blurb: Fast-renewable hardwood alternative with a distinctive linear grain
materials.description: Compressed bamboo strips give a board harder than most hardwoods, with a fine linear figure that finishes beautifully in oil. A strong sustainability story for worktops, shelving and table tops.

materials.name: Decorative laminate (HPL)
materials.blurb: Standard 1 mm high-pressure laminate — the industry default
materials.description: Kraft paper layers cured under heat and pressure with a decorative face. The 1 mm sheet is the baseline finish for wardrobes, kitchens and panelling, available in thousands of designs across every major brand.

materials.name: Solid colour laminate
materials.blurb: Flat, even colour with no pattern — the base of every modern palette
materials.description: Single-tone sheets in whites, greys, greiges and accent colours. The safest way to hold a scheme together across kitchen shutters, wardrobe fronts and loose furniture from different suppliers.

materials.name: Wood-finish laminate
materials.blurb: Printed timber grain, from pale oak to dark walnut
materials.description: The most-sold decor family in India: real timber photography printed and embossed in register so the texture follows the grain. Gives the warmth of veneer at a fraction of the cost and with none of the polishing.

materials.name: Stone & marble finish laminate
materials.blurb: Marble and stone reproductions for counters and cladding
materials.description: Book-matched marble and stone decors that read convincingly at arm's length. Used where a real slab is out of budget or out of weight limits — vanity fronts, feature walls and lift lobbies.

materials.name: Fabric-finish laminate
materials.blurb: Woven and linen textures for soft, tactile surfaces
materials.description: Textile decors with a matching embossed texture, giving panelling the softness of upholstery without the maintenance. Popular on bedbacks, wardrobe shutters and hospitality panelling.

materials.name: Metal-finish laminate
materials.blurb: Brushed brass, copper and steel looks without the metal
materials.description: Metallic decors — brushed gold, antique copper, gunmetal — printed on standard HPL. All the drama of a metal panel at a tenth of the weight and cost, though they show fingerprints unless specified anti-smudge.

materials.name: High-gloss laminate
materials.blurb: Mirror-level shine for kitchens and hall units
materials.description: A high-gloss overlay that reflects light and visually opens small rooms. Beautiful when new and unforgiving thereafter — every swirl mark shows, so pair it with anti-scratch grades and handle-less profiles.

materials.name: Matte laminate
materials.blurb: Low-sheen finish that hides marks and reads contemporary
materials.description: The current default in premium residential work: a 5–15 gloss unit surface that softens light, hides dust and photographs well. Best paired with anti-fingerprint technology in dark shades.

materials.name: Suede-finish laminate
materials.blurb: Velvety, ultra-low-sheen touch surface
materials.description: A fine micro-texture that feels like suede under the hand and kills reflection almost entirely. Specify for bedrooms and studies where a hard shine would feel wrong.

materials.name: Textured laminate
materials.blurb: Deep 3D surface texture you can feel — wood pore, slate, ribbed
materials.description: Heavy embossing that reproduces sawn timber, riven slate or fine ribs. Adds shadow and depth to large flat runs and disguises the flatness that gives cheap joinery away.

materials.name: Anti-fingerprint laminate
materials.blurb: Dark matte surfaces that stay clean-looking in daily use
materials.description: A surface treatment that stops skin oils leaving visible marks — essential on charcoal, navy and black matte shutters, which otherwise look smeared within a week of handover.

materials.name: Scratch-resistant laminate
materials.blurb: Hardened overlay for counters and high-traffic surfaces
materials.description: An extra-hard overlay resists the abrasion that ruins ordinary laminate on worktops, study desks and reception counters. Look for the brand's abrasion class rather than a marketing claim.

materials.name: Fire-retardant laminate
materials.blurb: Class-rated surface for commercial and public interiors
materials.description: Meets flame-spread requirements for offices, hotels and hospitals where fire consultants sign off the interior finishes. Same decors as the standard range, with a certified core.

materials.name: Exterior laminate
materials.blurb: UV-stable compact sheet for façades and balconies
materials.description: Weatherproof compact laminate engineered for direct sun and rain, with a warranted colour-fastness period. Used for façade cladding, balcony panels and external signage.

materials.name: Compact laminate
materials.blurb: Self-supporting solid sheet — no substrate needed
materials.description: Full-thickness HPL that needs no board behind it, with a black or coloured core at the edges. The standard for toilet cubicles, lab counters, lockers and wet-area partitions.

materials.name: Digital laminate
materials.blurb: Your artwork printed to sheet — murals, logos, custom decors
materials.description: Digitally printed HPL lets a client's artwork, a brand logo or a bespoke pattern become a durable surface. Minimum order quantities apply, so plan it into the drawing set early.

materials.name: Acrylic laminate
materials.blurb: Mirror-gloss acrylic face with depth no HPL can match
materials.description: A cast acrylic layer over a board substrate gives a deep, glassy reflection used on premium kitchens and wardrobes. Costs several times a gloss laminate and needs careful edge banding to look right.

materials.name: Edge band
materials.blurb: PVC or ABS banding that finishes and protects every cut edge
materials.description: The detail that separates good joinery from bad: matched banding sealed to the board edge stops moisture ingress and chipping. Specify 0.8 mm for visible edges and 2 mm on shutters that take daily knocks.

materials.name: Natural veneer
materials.blurb: Sliced from a real log — every leaf unique
materials.description: The genuine article: thin timber sliced from a log and laid on board. Colour and figure vary sheet to sheet, so order the full requirement from one bundle and plan the match on the drawing before cutting.

materials.name: Reconstituted veneer
materials.blurb: Engineered from fast-growing timber for a repeatable grain
materials.description: Fast-grown wood is dyed, laminated and re-sliced to a consistent grain, so sheet 40 matches sheet 1. The pragmatic choice for large runs, hotel rooms and anywhere the client cannot tolerate variation.

materials.name: Engineered veneer
materials.blurb: Designed grain patterns unavailable in nature
materials.description: Same technology as reconstituted veneer, used deliberately for graphic effect — extra-wide straight grain, tight ripple, colour-shifted greys. Gives a contemporary, controlled look no natural log will hold.

materials.name: Pre-finished veneer
materials.blurb: Factory-polished — no site polishing, no smell, no delay
materials.description: Arrives sealed and cured in a factory line, so the carpenter cuts, bands and installs with no polishing trade on site. Removes a week of dust and fumes from a live-in renovation.

materials.name: Teak veneer
materials.blurb: The Indian classic — warm gold-brown, ages beautifully
materials.description: Burma and African teak remain the default premium species in Indian homes, especially for main doors and pooja units. Rich golden brown when new, deepening with age and oil.

materials.name: Oak veneer
materials.blurb: Open-pore, pale and contemporary — the current favourite
materials.description: European and American oak in natural, smoked and white-washed variants. The open pore reads beautifully in matte finishes and suits the pale Scandinavian palettes clients keep asking for.

materials.name: Walnut veneer
materials.blurb: Deep chocolate brown with dramatic figure
materials.description: American walnut brings depth and quiet luxury — the species to specify for a study, a bar or a formal living room. Expensive, and worth planning the layout around so the figure runs continuously.

materials.name: Ash veneer
materials.blurb: Very pale, strong grain — excellent under stain
materials.description: Almost white with a pronounced grain that takes stain evenly, so it can be pushed grey, black or warm without losing figure. A designer's blank canvas.

materials.name: Maple veneer
materials.blurb: Fine, near-uniform grain in a creamy blond
materials.description: Subtle and even — used where the timber should recede and the form should lead. Popular in minimal wardrobes and kids' rooms where a busy grain would be a distraction.

materials.name: Rosewood veneer
materials.blurb: Dark, richly figured Indian classic for statement joinery
materials.description: Sheesham and allied species deliver deep purple-brown tones with strong dark streaks. Traditional in Indian homes for door panels and heirloom furniture; check the source paperwork on protected species.

materials.name: Mahogany veneer
materials.blurb: Warm reddish brown with a fine ribbon figure
materials.description: A traditional joinery timber with a red undertone that warms a room under yellow light. Suits classical detailing, panelled libraries and period-reference work.

materials.name: Ebony veneer
materials.blurb: Near-black timber for the strongest contrast in a scheme
materials.description: Dense, dark and expensive — used in slivers rather than sheets. A single ebony reveal or handle detail does more work than an entire wall of a cheaper species.

materials.name: Smoked veneer
materials.blurb: Fumed timber — colour driven right through the sheet
materials.description: Ammonia fuming darkens the wood chemically rather than with stain, so the tone runs through the leaf and sanding will not expose a pale line. Gives smoked oak its characteristic depth.

materials.name: Acrylic sheet
materials.blurb: Cast acrylic panel with a glass-like reflection
materials.description: A solid cast acrylic layer bonded to board gives the deepest gloss available in modular joinery. Reads almost like lacquered glass, and unlike gloss laminate it can be polished if it scratches.

materials.name: PET sheet
materials.blurb: Recyclable gloss panel with better scratch behaviour than acrylic
materials.description: PET gives a comparable shine to acrylic with a harder, more scratch-tolerant face and a stronger recycling story. Increasingly specified where sustainability is on the client brief.

materials.name: High-gloss panel (pre-laminated)
materials.blurb: Board that arrives finished on both faces, edges banded
materials.description: A ready-to-fit panel — gloss face, balanced back, matching 2 mm band. Removes the pressing and banding steps from a tight programme and guarantees a factory-flat surface.

materials.name: Anti-fingerprint panel
materials.blurb: Matte or gloss surface treated to shrug off smudges
materials.description: A nano-coating that stops fingerprints registering on dark surfaces. On a handle-less charcoal kitchen this is not a luxury — it is the difference between a photograph and a smear.

materials.name: Matte acrylic
materials.blurb: The softness of suede with the depth of acrylic
materials.description: Acrylic's solid colour depth in a low-sheen finish — currently the most requested premium kitchen surface. Pairs well with fluted timber and stone counters.

materials.name: Metallic acrylic
materials.blurb: Metal-effect gloss for bars, retail and statement units
materials.description: Champagne, bronze and gunmetal acrylics with a mirrored metallic depth. Strong in small doses — a bar front or a single wardrobe bay — and overwhelming across a whole room.
